  DRAFTS:
  DRAFT 1 (impact; 251/1449 chars)
  ONE SENTENCE: Poodle is a claims desk for car insurers: it watches the dashcam video of a crash, checks the driver's statement against what the camera saw, works out what the policy pays with fixed rules, and refers anything it is not sure about to a human handler.
  DESCRIPTION:
  After a crash, a claims handler watches the dashcam clip, reads the statement and checks the policy by hand. Poodle does that first pass for car insurers. The claim page shows real footage with YOLO boxes on the cars, the driver's statement checked line by line (supported, contradicted or unverifiable), and a recommendation with the policy clause or Highway Code rule behind each reason. Every file gets a SHA-256 hash; it prints as a one-page evidence pack.
  
  Code owns dates, money and the decision table. TypeSafe Jev answers nine typed questions per claim, such as fault and fraud risk, each with a confidence. Under 0.5 on a key answer the claim goes to a person, and the page says why. Accepts up to £1,500 settle straight through.
  
  It also watches about 800 TfL JamCams. Each new still goes to Jev with 12 questions plus a box in one call; a score of 0.7 opens an incident and a second still confirms it. All of London costs about $0.50 an hour.
  
  Cursor wrote the product commits; Claude Code helped. NVIDIA: a Cosmos Reason adapter answers questions from the clip; YOLO uses the lab endpoint when its URL is set, else local YOLO11s. CoreWeave: a W&B Inference adapter answers from the findings. VAST Data: every question, action and incident event goes to a VastDB events table. These switch on from env vars; we had no credentials on the build laptop, so Cosmos, W&B and VastDB are written but not tested and the desk falls back to replay.
  CAVEATS: Statement check verdicts (supported / contradicted / unverifiable) are hand-written seed data in server/data/claims.json; no code computes them. The description says the page shows the statement 'checked line by line', which is what the UI renders, but a judge reading the code will see the verdicts are seeded. README.md:206 admits this ('The findings, statement checks and Jev answers were written for each clip'). Consider adding 'from recorded findings' if space allows. | 'YOLO uses the lab endpoint when its URL is set' is wired but unverified: the YOLO_URL request shape (POST /v1/infer with image_base64) is listed as unverified in the services.py docstring. Only the local Ultralytics YOLO11s path has actually run. YOLO11s is an Ultralytics model, not an NVIDIA product; the NVIDIA link is the lab endpoint and the Cosmos adapter. | The CoreWeave (W&B) tag covers only the W&B Inference adapter. There is no Weave tracing, no evals and no logged metrics anywhere in the code (grep for 'weave' finds nothing). I did not claim any of these. | VastDB usage is a single-row insert into one events table with a JSON payload. Nothing reads from VastDB, and clips and stills are not stored there (they live on local disk under server/data/library/). The description's 'every question, action and incident event goes to a VastDB events table' is the written behaviour, untested. Do not say clips or decisions live in VastDB. | 'About 800 TfL JamCams' and '$0.50 an hour' are README figures. Today's runtime log (gitignored, not in the repo) shows 819 distinct cameras judged, 11,399 frames and about $0.81 of Jev tokens in roughly 70 minutes, so the real rate is higher than the README estimate. I left runtime numbers out per the rule that numbers come from code or README; tfl.py's docstring says ~890 cameras and a Cursor commit says 811. | Cursor did not write 'most commits' numerically: 12 of 28 are cursor:, 11 are claude-code:, 4 are GitHub-web uploads, 1 is bootstrap. The Cursor commits do carry the product milestones, so the text says 'product commits'. | 'Accepts up to £1,500 settle straight through' is the rule in engine.py and policies.json (autoSettle 1500 on all 8 policies). In replay mode only one of the 8 claims (PD-0226, payable £1,040) actually settles straight through, and README:200 says live Jev is stricter and refers most claims. No live-Jev claim outcome is claimed. | No precision or accuracy figure is claimed for the scanner. Today's library has 0 incidents labelled verified and 6 dismissed, so none can be. README:183 states a threshold test (crash stills 0.94-0.99, highest normal still 0.63) but the raw data for it is not in the repo; I left it out for space. | The services.py docstring lists the Jev request shape as unverified, while README:200 says live Jev has been run with a key. I followed the README and treated Jev as live-with-key; the Jev key is not in the repo. | The Cosmos Reason adapter returns no citations (citations hard-coded to []), so 'answers questions from the clip' is correct but finding-level grounding comes only from the W&B and replay paths. Both Cosmos and W&B adapters have never been executed against a real endpoint. | 'Every file gets a SHA-256 hash' is true, but the custody loggedAt timestamps for the three seed files per claim are synthetic offsets (reportedAt + 3, 4, 5 s); only attached camera stills use the real clock. | Not built and not mentioned: multi-camera sync, bird's-eye reconstruction, speed estimation, Canary ASR, VSS search, cross-claim vector search, face/plate blurring, automatic threshold calibration from review labels. The description names none of them. | Lengths: one sentence 251 characters; description 1,449 characters including the three blank-line separators (limit 1,450). If the form counts differently, the safest cut is 'and the page says why' (22 characters).

  DRAFT 2 (technical; 289/1443 chars)
  ONE SENTENCE: Poodle is a claims desk for motor insurers that turns a dashcam clip into a decision: YOLO boxes and timed findings, TypeSafe Jev typed answers with confidences, a code table that pays, refers or rejects, and a SHA-256 evidence pack showing why; it also watches about 800 live TfL cameras.
  DESCRIPTION:
  Poodle is a claims desk for motor insurers. A handler sees the dashcam clip, YOLO11s boxes and timed findings. Findings, statement and policy go to TypeSafe Jev as nine closed questions (peril, fault, exclusion, fraud), each answered with a confidence. Code owns the rest: hard rules on dates, registration, driver and territory, then a decision table that pays, refers or rejects. A key confidence under 0.5 sends the claim to a person; a reject needs 0.9. Reasons cite clauses or Highway Code rules, files get SHA-256 hashes, and it prints as one evidence pack.
  
  It also watches London: it polls about 800 TfL JamCams and sends each new still to Jev with 12 batched questions plus a box for where it is. Code tracks state per camera: one flagged frame opens an incident, a second confirms it, two quiet frames clear it; stills and 10-second clips are kept. Today it judged about 11,000 stills from 819 cameras, median 260 ms each.
  
  NVIDIA: YOLO11s boxes claim footage and live stills, locally or on the lab YOLO endpoint; a Cosmos Reason adapter answers from the clip. CoreWeave (W&B): a W&B Inference adapter answers from the findings. VAST Data: every question, action and incident goes to a VastDB table. SpaceXAI (Cursor): Cursor wrote most of the code, sharing a taskboard with Claude Code. The lab YOLO, Cosmos, W&B and VastDB adapters switch on from env vars and are untested; without keys Poodle falls back to replay and a local log.
  CAVEATS: 'A reject needs 0.9' is the bar for the two Jev-driven reject branches (exclusion confidence >= 0.9, or section_covers_peril < 0.5 with Noul confidence >= 0.9). Hard-rule rejects (driver not named, out of UK territory, policy not in force, reg mismatch) need no confidence at all. If a judge probes, say so. | 'Findings, statement and policy go to TypeSafe Jev' describes the wiring in services.jev_decide. In the demo without a key, the nine answers are the recorded ones in claims.json and the decision record says mode 'seeded'. README says live Jev was run with a key and is stricter (sends most claims to a person); the services.py docstring still lists the Jev claim request shape as unverified. Only the scanner's live Jev use is proven by today's observation file. | 'About 11,000 stills from 819 cameras, median 260 ms' was counted at 16:12 BST from server/data/library/observations-2026-10-17.jsonl (11,380 rows, 819 distinct cams, median 259 ms, median 1,701 tokens). Those files are gitignored runtime state and the scanner was still running, so the figure will have grown and a judge cannot reproduce it from the repo. | 'About 800 TfL JamCams' is the README wording. tfl.py says ~890, 819 were judged today, cams.json holds state for 711; the number is whatever TfL marks available at poll time. | 'Locally or on the lab YOLO endpoint': only the local Ultralytics path has been run. The YOLO_URL adapter (POST /v1/infer with image_base64) is unverified, which is why the last sentence lists the lab YOLO adapter among the untested ones. | 'A Cosmos Reason adapter answers from the clip' is the untested Q&A path only. The 25 findings labelled 'Cosmos (replay)' in claims.json are hand-written seed text, not Cosmos output; the copy deliberately does not say Cosmos produced the findings. | 'Every question, action and incident goes to a VastDB table' is wiring, untested, and write-only: nothing reads from VastDB, and clips and stills are not stored there, only event rows with a JSON payload. | Statement check verdicts (supported/contradicted/unverifiable) are seeded in claims.json and only counted and rendered; no code computes them. The copy mentions the statement only as Jev input (true: statement text is in the Jev state) and does not claim automated statement verification. | No scanner precision figure is claimed because none exists: 0 incidents are labelled 'verified' today, 6 'dismissed', and threshold calibration from review labels is manual (watch.py:40-42). | 'Cursor wrote most of the code' rests on 12 cursor vs 11 claude-code commits, where the cursor commits carry the product milestones and most claude-code commits are hook checkpoints and docs. 4 untagged commits by Ravi K came through the GitHub web UI. | Nothing from docs/IDEA.md that is not in code was used: no multi-camera sync, bird's-eye reconstruction, Weave evals, Canary ASR, VSS search, cross-claim vector search, face/plate blurring or decision letters. grep for weave/vss/canary/embed in server/ and poodle/js returns nothing. | Character counts: one sentence 289/290, description 1,443/1,450 including the two blank lines. Three paragraphs, plain text, no em dashes, no bullets.

```text
### Live cameras

![Live TfL cameras, grouped by the claim they are near](docs/screens/cameras.jpg)

Every claim gets the four Transport for London (TfL) traffic cameras closest to it, with distances. London has about 800 of these cameras, and they post a new picture every 5 to 8 minutes.

![A live camera scanned with YOLO: 1 bus, 10 cars, 2 traffic lights and 1 person, next to an "Attach as evidence" button](docs/screens/live-scan.jpg)

Open a camera and scan its latest picture with YOLO. If it helps, attach it to a claim. The picture gets a fingerprint and goes into the claim's evidence log.

### The incident library
----
| --- | --- | --- |
| London traffic cameras | No key needed (`TFL_APP_KEY` raises TfL's rate limit) | The last saved camera list |
| YOLO scan of a live camera | `YOLO_URL`, or `ultralytics` installed locally | The scan says no detector is connected |
| Boxes on the claim footage | Worked out ahead of time with YOLO11s (`server/tools/detect_stills.py`) | Same |
| Coverage decision | `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` or `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` (Jev) | Recorded Jev answers |
| Questions about the footage | `COSMOS3_REASON_URL` (Cosmos Reason) or `WANDB_API_KEY` (W&B Inference) | Answers built from the findings |
| Incident library | A Jev key | Off |
| Event store | `VASTDB_ENDPOINT`, `VASTDB_ACCESS_KEY` and `VASTDB_SECRET_KEY` | `server/data/events.jsonl` |
----
The scanner is in `server/watch.py`. Here's what it does.

1. About once a minute it asks each camera whether its picture has changed. A picture that hasn't changed costs nothing.
2. A new picture goes to Jev once, with 12 questions in a single request. Is there an incident? What kind? Is a lane blocked? Is the road wet? There are eight more like these, plus a box around the problem.
3. One picture that scores 0.7 or more, with an incident type such as a collision or a breakdown, opens an incident. A second picture confirms it.
4. Two quiet pictures in a row close it. So do 30 minutes with no new picture.

Every judged picture also goes into a daily log. That gives you road conditions and traffic for every camera in London, every few minutes. It all lives in `server/data/library/`, which isn't committed and is served at `/library/`.

| File | What's in it |
| --- | --- |
| `observations-<date>.jsonl` | One line per picture: camera, time, every answer, tokens used |
| `incidents.json` | The incident library (the Export button downloads it) |
| `frames/` and `clips/` | Incident pictures and 10-second clips, each with a SHA-256 hash |

Opened, confirmed, cleared and reviewed incidents also go to `events.jsonl`, and to VastDB once it's set up.

### What it costs

A picture costs about 1,700 Jev tokens, roughly $0.00007. All of London comes to about 7,000 pictures and $0.50 an hour.

### How to control it

----

### Why the threshold is 0.7

In a test, real crash pictures scored between 0.94 and 0.99. The highest normal London picture in the first sweep scored 0.63, and that was a smudged lens. So 0.7 sits in the gap. Some sun glare still gets through, which is why the review buttons are there. The questions and thresholds are all at the top of `server/watch.py`.

## Demo in 90 seconds

1. The inbox has seven claims that need a person. Open PD-0147 (`J`/`K`, then `Enter`).
2. The policyholder's dashcam plays. A blue Vauxhall Mokka pulls out of a give-way junction into her. Click the finding "Blue car broadside across the policyholder's lane" and the clip stops there, with a YOLO box on the car. The two nearest live TfL cameras sit beside it.
3. Ask "Where was the point of impact?" (the answer cites the impact finding). Then ask "How fast was the other car going?" (the answer is "Not visible").
4. The recommendation is accept, partial. The other driver is at fault under Highway Code rule 172, and the courtesy car isn't on her policy. Poodle pays £6,500 now and recovers £6,850 from the other insurer.
5. Open a live camera, scan its latest picture and attach it to the claim. It joins the evidence log with its fingerprint.
6. Press `⌘K` and type "camden". PD-0226 (hit from behind in traffic) can be paid without a handler. PD-0188 (a car cut in from a slip road, then braked hard) has a fraud flag and goes to the special investigations team. In PD-0204 the van driver says he was already on the roundabout, and the rider's helmet camera says he wasn't.
7. Press `G` then `L` for the incident library: the scanner's live feed and the incidents it found today.
8. Open the evidence pack: one printable page with the decision, the findings, the statement check and the file fingerprints.

The amounts in steps 4 and 6 come from the recorded Jev answers. See the next section.

## What doesn't work yet

- Live Jev is stricter than the recorded answers. With a Jev key set, it sends most claims to a person for now.
- The incident scanner has false alarms, mostly sun glare and dirty lenses.
- The Cosmos Reason, W&B Inference and VastDB connections are written but not tested. We didn't have those credentials on the laptop we built this on.

## Where the footage comes from

The claim videos are real UK dashcam and helmet-camera clips sent in to UK Dash Cameras. The originals are in `poodle/media/raw/` (about 90 MB). `server/tools/build_media.py` cuts them into 720p web clips with posters (about 16 MB). The findings, statement checks and Jev answers were written for each clip. The places, dates, people and policies are made up, so the dates burned into the videos don't match the claims.

Live camera pictures come from TfL JamCams. Powered by TfL Open Data.

We also tried generating crash clips. `server/tools/luma_videos.py` makes 5-second CCTV-style clips with Luma Ray2 on Amazon Bedrock, with the camera locked in place. The desk doesn't use them. It plays the real footage. Ray2 only runs in us-west-2, costs $7.50 per clip and needs `aws sso login`.

## Deploying
```

```text
# Submission form copy

Texts for the Real-Time Video Agents Hack form (VAST London, 17 Oct 2026). Plain English, no em dashes.
Every claim matches the code as of this commit. Cosmos Reason, W&B Inference and VastDB are wired in but
were never run with credentials, and the text says so.

## One-sentence description (221/300 characters)

Poodle is a claims desk for car insurers that watches the dashcam video of a crash, checks the driver's story against what the camera saw, works out what the policy pays, and hands anything it isn't sure about to a human.

## Project description (1448/1,500 characters)

Poodle helps car insurance handlers decide claims from video. A handler opens a claim and sees the real dashcam clip with YOLO boxes on the cars, a timeline of what happened, and the driver's statement checked line by line: supported, contradicted or unverifiable. They can ask the footage questions, and every answer cites a finding or says "Not visible". The recommendation shows what's covered and what to pay, with the policy clause or Highway Code rule behind each reason. Every file gets a SHA-256 hash, and it all prints as a one-page evidence pack.

How it decides: code owns the rules, dates and money. TypeSafe Jev answers closed questions (what happened, who was at fault, fraud risk) with a confidence score. Under 50% sure, Poodle refers the claim to a person and says why.

It also watches London. It polls about 800 TfL traffic cameras and sends each new still to Jev with 12 image questions in one call. Code turns the answers into an incident library with stills, 10-second clips and review buttons, and logs road conditions per camera every few minutes. All of London costs about $0.50 an hour.

Tools: YOLO11s finds vehicles in claim footage and live stills. We built it in Cursor and Claude Code, which shared one taskboard. Cosmos Reason (video Q&A), W&B Inference (answers) and VastDB (event store) are wired in and switch on with credentials. We had none on build day, so the demo uses recorded answers and a local event log.

Optional bold in the form: the lead-ins "How it decides:", "It also watches London." and "Tools:".

## Technologies, and where each one is in the code

| Technology | How Poodle uses it | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cursor | Built the app; shared taskboard with Claude Code | `agent-coordination/`, `.cursor/` |
| TypeSafe Jev | Coverage answers on claims; 12 image questions per TfL still | `server/services.py`, `server/watch.py` |
| YOLO11s (Ultralytics) | Boxes on claim footage (precomputed) and live camera scans | `server/tools/detect_stills.py`, `server/services.py` |
| TfL JamCams | About 800 live London cameras | `server/tfl.py`, `server/watch.py` |
| NVIDIA Cosmos Reason | Video Q&A when `COSMOS3_REASON_URL` is set (not run on build day) | `server/services.py` |
| W&B Inference | Plain-English answers when `WANDB_API_KEY` is set (not run on build day) | `server/services.py` |
| VAST (VastDB) | Event store when `VASTDB_ENDPOINT` is set (not run on build day) | `server/services.py` |
```

```text
def activity(claim: dict, decision: dict) -> list[dict]:
    t0 = datetime.fromisoformat(claim["reportedAt"])
    dets = DETECTIONS[claim["id"]]["detections"]
    counts = Counter(d["label"] for d in dets)

        (0, "Poodle", f"Opened the claim from {claim['channel'].lower()}."),

def record_event(event: dict) -> None:
    event = {"at": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S"), **event}
    with EVENTS.open("a") as f:
        f.write(json.dumps(event) + "\n")
    if env("VASTDB_ENDPOINT"):
        try:
            _vastdb_insert(event)
        except Exception as exc:  # keep the desk working if the store is down
            print("vastdb insert failed:", exc)


def _vastdb_insert(event: dict) -> None:
    import pyarrow as pa
    import vastdb

    session = vastdb.connect(endpoint=env("VASTDB_ENDPOINT"), access=env("VASTDB_ACCESS_KEY"), secret=env("VASTDB_SECRET_KEY"))
    columns = pa.schema([("at", pa.string()), ("claim", pa.string()), ("kind", pa.string()), ("payload", pa.string())])
    with session.transaction() as tx:
        bucket = tx.bucket(env("VASTDB_BUCKET") or "poodle")
        schema = bucket.schema("poodle", fail_if_missing=False) or bucket.create_schema("poodle")
        table = schema.table("events", fail_if_missing=False) or schema.create_table("events", columns)
        table.insert(pa.table({"at": [event["at"]], "claim": [event.get("claim", "")], "kind": [event.get("kind", "")],
                               "payload": [json.dumps(event)]}))


def services_status(tfl_status: dict) -> list[dict]:
    def s(id_, name, role, live, live_text, fallback):
        return {"id": id_, "name": name, "role": role, "status": "live" if live else "replay", "detail": live_text if live else fallback}

    yolo_live = bool(env("YOLO_URL")) or LOCAL_YOLO
    try:
        import vastdb  # noqa: F401
        vastdb_sdk = True
    except Exception:
        vastdb_sdk = False
    vastdb_fallback = "SDK not installed (pip install vastdb pyarrow)" if env("VASTDB_ENDPOINT") else "Local event log"
    return [
        s("tfl", "TfL JamCams", "Live London cameras", tfl_status["ok"], f"{tfl_status['count']} live", "Snapshot (feed unreachable)"),
        s("yolo", "YOLO11", "Detection on frames", yolo_live, "Event stack" if env("YOLO_URL") else "Local yolo11s", "Precomputed boxes"),
        s("cosmos", "Cosmos Reason", "Video reasoning", bool(env("COSMOS3_REASON_URL")), "Event stack", "Recorded findings"),
        s("jev", "TypeSafe Jev", "Typed coverage answers", bool(env("TYPESAFE_API_KEY") or env("OPENROUTER_API_KEY")), "jev-1.14.0", "Seeded answers"),
        s("llm", "W&B Inference", "Answers in plain English", bool(env("WANDB_API_KEY")), env("POODLE_LLM_MODEL") or "Llama 3.3 70B", "Rule-based answers"),
        s("vastdb", "VastDB", "Evidence and events store", bool(env("VASTDB_ENDPOINT")) and vastdb_sdk, "Writing events", vastdb_fallback),
    ]
```

  FINAL COPY:
  ONE SENTENCE (269 chars): Poodle is a claims desk for car insurers that watches the dashcam clip of a crash, sets the driver's statement beside what the camera saw, works out what the policy pays with fixed rules and typed Jev answers, and sends anything it is not sure about to a human handler.
  
  DESCRIPTION (1426 chars):
  After a crash, a handler watches the dashcam clip, reads the statement and checks the policy by hand. Poodle does that first pass for car insurers. The claim page shows the clip with YOLO11s boxes, timed findings and the driver's statement. Footage answers cite a finding or say "Not visible". Every file is SHA-256 hashed; it prints as one evidence pack.
  
  Code runs hard checks on dates, registration, driver and territory, then a decision table pays, refers or rejects. TypeSafe Jev answers nine typed questions per claim (peril, fault, exclusion, fraud), each with a confidence. Under 0.5 on a key answer the claim goes to a person; a Jev-driven reject needs 0.9.
  
  It also watches about 800 TfL JamCams. Each new still goes to Jev with 12 questions in one call, including a box. Code tracks each camera: a frame at 0.7 opens an incident, a second confirms it, two quiet frames clear it. Stills, 10-second clips, every answer and review verdicts sit in one library. All of London costs about $0.50 an hour.
  
  NVIDIA: Cosmos Reason video Q&A, plus YOLO on the lab endpoint or local YOLO11s. CoreWeave (Weights & Biases): W&B Inference answers from the findings. VAST Data: every question, action and incident goes to VastDB. SpaceXAI (Cursor): Cursor wrote most of the code. Lab YOLO, Cosmos, W&B and VastDB switch on from env vars and are untested (no credentials on build day); the desk falls back to replay and a local log.
  
  TAGS: NVIDIA, CoreWeave (Weights & Biases), VAST Data, SpaceXAI (Cursor) + TfL JamCams, TypeSafe Jev, YOLO11, Ultralytics, FastAPI, Claude Code, Insurance claims, Dashcam

  ONE SENTENCE (269 chars): Poodle is a claims desk for car insurers that watches the dashcam clip of a crash, sets the driver's statement beside what the camera saw, works out what the policy pays with fixed rules and typed Jev answers, and sends anything it is not sure about to a human handler.
  
  DESCRIPTION (1426 chars):
  After a crash, a handler watches the dashcam clip, reads the statement and checks the policy by hand. Poodle does that first pass for car insurers. The claim page shows the clip with YOLO11s boxes, timed findings and the driver's statement. Footage answers cite a finding or say "Not visible". Every file is SHA-256 hashed; it prints as one evidence pack.
  
  Code runs hard checks on dates, registration, driver and territory, then a decision table pays, refers or rejects. TypeSafe Jev answers nine typed questions per claim (peril, fault, exclusion, fraud), each with a confidence. Under 0.5 on a key answer the claim goes to a person; a Jev-driven reject needs 0.9.
  
  It also watches about 800 TfL JamCams. Each new still goes to Jev with 12 questions in one call, including a box. Code tracks each camera: a frame at 0.7 opens an incident, a second confirms it, two quiet frames clear it. Stills, 10-second clips, every answer and review verdicts sit in one library. All of London costs about $0.50 an hour.
  
  NVIDIA: Cosmos Reason video Q&A, plus YOLO on the lab endpoint or local YOLO11s. CoreWeave (Weights & Biases): W&B Inference answers from the findings. VAST Data: every question, action and incident goes to VastDB. SpaceXAI (Cursor): Cursor wrote most of the code. Lab YOLO, Cosmos, W&B and VastDB switch on from env vars and are untested (no credentials on build day); the desk falls back to replay and a local log.
  
  TAGS: NVIDIA, CoreWeave (Weights & Biases), VAST Data, SpaceXAI (Cursor) + TfL JamCams, TypeSafe Jev, YOLO11, Ultralytics, FastAPI, Claude Code, Insurance claims, Dashcam

```text
import httpx

from . import services, tfl

LIBRARY = Path(services.env("POODLE_LIBRARY_DIR") or Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "data" / "library")
USD_PER_TOKEN = 0.042 / 1_000_000

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- questions and thresholds
# One reviewable place for what Jev is asked about each frame and how code acts on it.
# Thresholds are starting points from a probe on crash stills and live frames; calibrate
# them on the review labels the desk collects.

QUESTIONS = {
    "usable": {
        "type": "noul", "instructions": "Can the road and the vehicles on it be seen in `frame`?",
        "criteria": {"true": "the carriageway is visible clearly enough to judge what is happening on it",
                     "false": "the frame is blank, grey, a 'camera unavailable' card, pointing at a wall or the sky, "
                              "too dark to see the road, or the lens is covered by rain, glare or dirt"}},
    "incident": {
        "type": "noul", "instructions": "Does `frame` show a road incident happening now?",
        "criteria": {"true": "a collision, a damaged, overturned or burning vehicle, a vehicle stopped across a live lane "
                             "or at an odd angle, emergency services working on the road, debris or a fallen object on "
                             "the carriageway, flooding, or a person lying in the road",
                     "false": "ordinary traffic, including queues, parked cars, buses at stops, vehicles waiting at lights, "
                              "roadworks behind barriers, and vehicles stopped at the kerb"}},
    "kind": {
        "type": "choice", "instructions": "What is the main thing happening on the road in `frame`?",
        "criteria": {
            "collision": "a crash: vehicles in contact, a damaged or overturned vehicle, or wreckage",
            "breakdown": "one vehicle stopped in a live lane with hazard lights, a raised bonnet or a tow truck",
            "emergency_response": "police, ambulance or fire vehicles stopped on the road at a scene",
            "obstruction": "debris, a fallen tree, a spilled load or another object blocking the carriageway",
            "flooding": "standing water covering part of the carriageway",
            "fire_or_smoke": "flames or smoke from a vehicle or the roadside",
            "person_in_road": "a person lying, standing or walking in a live traffic lane away from a crossing",
            "roadworks": "planned works: cones, barriers, works vehicles or a lane closed for maintenance",
            "congestion": "slow or stationary queues with no visible cause",
            "normal": "traffic moving normally, or an empty road",
            "unclear": "the frame is too dark, blurred, obstructed or blank to tell",
            "other": "something else unusual on the road"}},
    "severity": {
        "type": "score", "instructions": "How urgently should a traffic control room operator look at `frame`?",
        "criteria": ["nothing to act on: normal traffic",
                     "worth noting: a stopped vehicle, a queue or works that is not blocking traffic",
                     "act now: a lane is blocked by a collision, breakdown, obstruction or emergency scene",
                     "major: a serious crash, a fire, an overturned vehicle, people hurt, or the road is closed"]},
    "emergency_vehicle": {"type": "noul", "instructions": "Is a police car, ambulance or fire engine visible in `frame`?"},
    "damaged_vehicle": {
        "type": "noul",
        "instructions": "Is a vehicle in `frame` visibly damaged, overturned, on fire, or facing against the flow of traffic?"},
    "lane_blocked": {
        "type": "noul",
        "instructions": "Is a traffic lane in `frame` blocked by a stopped vehicle, debris, people or emergency services, "
                        "so that traffic has to go around it?",
        "criteria": {"true": "a lane is obstructed by something that is not part of normal traffic",
                     "false": "vehicles waiting at lights or in a queue, parked in bays, or at a bus stop; or no lane is blocked"}},
    "people_in_road": {
        "type": "noul", "instructions": "Are people standing or walking in a traffic lane in `frame`, away from a pedestrian crossing?"},
    "traffic": {
        "type": "score", "instructions": "How much traffic is on the road in `frame`?",
        "criteria": ["empty road", "light traffic with large gaps", "busy, vehicles close together",
                     "nose-to-tail queue filling the lanes"]},
    "surface": {
        "type": "choice", "instructions": "What is the condition of the road surface in `frame`?",
        "criteria": {"dry": "dry road", "wet": "wet road, puddles or reflections on the surface",
                     "snow_or_ice": "snow or ice on the road", "unclear": "cannot see the surface"}},
    "light": {
        "type": "choice", "instructions": "What is the lighting in `frame`?",
        "criteria": {"daylight": "daylight", "dusk": "dusk or dawn", "night_lit": "night with street lights",
                     "dark": "night without useful light"}},
    "where": {"type": "box",
              "instructions": "the collision, damaged vehicle, stopped vehicle, obstruction or emergency scene in `frame`"},
}

THRESHOLDS = {
    "usable": 0.5,  # below: the view cannot be judged, so the frame neither extends nor clears an incident
    "open": 0.7,    # `incident` needed to open an incident, or to count towards confirming one
    "keep": 0.5,    # `incident` that keeps an open incident alive
    "box": 0.3,     # weakest box confidence worth drawing
}
INCIDENT_KINDS = {"collision", "breakdown", "emergency_response", "obstruction", "flooding", "fire_or_smoke",
                  "person_in_road", "other"}
CONFIRM_FRAMES = 2       # flagged frames that confirm an incident
CLEAR_FRAMES = 2         # quiet frames in a row that clear it
STALE_SECONDS = 30 * 60  # an open incident with no frame for this long is cleared
MAX_FRAMES = 12          # stills kept per incident
MAX_CLIPS = 3            # 10 s clips kept per incident
POLL_IDLE = 60           # seconds between checks while a camera's still is unchanged
POLL_AFTER_NEW = 210     # TfL refreshes each camera every 5 to 8 minutes
FETCH_CONCURRENCY = 12
CENTRE = (51.5073, -0.1276)  # Charing Cross: POODLE_WATCH_LIMIT keeps the cameras nearest to it


def flagged(o: dict) -> bool:
    return o["usable"] >= THRESHOLDS["usable"] and o["incident"] >= THRESHOLDS["open"] and o["kind"] in INCIDENT_KINDS


def compact(a: dict) -> dict:
    """The typed answers for one frame, flattened into an observation row."""
    r = lambda x: round(float(x), 3)  # noqa: E731
    return {
        "usable": r(a["usable"]["noul"]), "incident": r(a["incident"]["noul"]),
        "kind": a["kind"]["choice"], "kindConf": r(a["kind"]["confidence"]),
        "severity": r(a["severity"]["score"]),
        "emergency": r(a["emergency_vehicle"]["noul"]), "damaged": r(a["damaged_vehicle"]["noul"]),
        "blocked": r(a["lane_blocked"]["noul"]), "people": r(a["people_in_road"]["noul"]),
        "traffic": r(a["traffic"]["score"]), "surface": a["surface"]["choice"], "light": a["light"]["choice"],
    }
```

```text
FAULT_OPTIONS = {
    "not_at_fault": "the policyholder did nothing to cause the collision",
    "shared_fault": "both drivers contributed",
    "mostly_at_fault": "the policyholder caused most of it",
    "fully_at_fault": "the policyholder caused it",
    "cannot_determine": "the facts do not show who caused it",
}


def jev_questions(policy: dict, wording: dict) -> dict:
    exclusions = {k: v["text"] for k, v in wording.items() if k.startswith("E")}
    exclusions["none"] = "no exclusion applies"
    return {
        "peril": {"type": "choice", "instructions": "What happened in `facts`?", "criteria": {
            "collision_with_vehicle": "a collision with another vehicle", "collision_with_object": "hit an object",
            "collision_with_pedestrian_or_cyclist": "hit a person on foot or a cyclist", "theft": "theft",
            "vandalism": "vandalism", "fire": "fire", "weather": "weather damage", "glass_only": "glass only", "other": "something else"}},
        "section_covers_peril": {"type": "noul", "instructions": "Does Section 1 in `policy` cover damage to the policyholder's own car for this incident under `policy.cover`?"},
        "exclusion": {"type": "choice", "instructions": "Which exclusion in `policy` do `facts` trigger?", "criteria": exclusions},
        "fault_band": {"type": "choice", "instructions": "How much did the policyholder contribute to the collision in `facts`?", "criteria": FAULT_OPTIONS},
        "benefit_courtesy_car": {"type": "noul", "instructions": "Would the policyholder need a courtesy car while their car is repaired, given `facts`?"},
        "benefit_legal_expenses": {"type": "noul", "instructions": "Do `facts` give the policyholder uninsured losses to recover from another driver?"},
        "severity": {"type": "score", "instructions": "How badly damaged is the policyholder's car in `facts`?",
                     "criteria": ["cosmetic scuffs", "repairable damage", "major structural damage", "likely write-off"]},
        "evidence_sufficient": {"type": "noul", "instructions": "Do `facts` contain enough evidence to decide cover without asking for more?"},
        "fraud_risk": {"type": "score", "instructions": "How strongly do `facts` match staged-collision patterns?",
                       "criteria": ["no staged-collision signs", "some signs worth a look", "strong staged-collision signs"]},
    }


def jev_target() -> tuple[str, str, str] | None:
    """(base URL, key, model) for Jev, or None when no key is set."""
    key = env("TYPESAFE_API_KEY") or env("OPENROUTER_API_KEY")
    if not key:
        return None
    direct = bool(env("TYPESAFE_API_KEY"))
    base = env("JEV_BASE_URL") or ("https://api.typesafe.ai" if direct else "https://openrouter.ai/api")
    model = env("JEV_MODEL") or ("jev-1.14.0" if direct else "typesafe/jev-1.14")
    return base, key, model


async def jev_decide(client: httpx.AsyncClient, claim: dict, policy: dict, wording: dict) -> dict | None:
    target = jev_target()
    if not target:
        return None
    base, key, model = target
    state = {
        "facts": {"findings": [f["text"] for f in claim["findings"]], "statement": claim["statement"]["text"],
                  "driver": claim["driver"], "estimate": claim.get("estimate")},
        "policy": {"cover": policy["cover"], "addOns": policy["addOns"],
                   "wording": {k: v["text"] for k, v in wording.items()}},
    }
    r = await client.post(f"{base}/v1/systemone", headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {key}"}, timeout=15,
                          json={"model": model, "state": state, "questions": jev_questions(policy, wording)})
    r.raise_for_status()
    a = r.json()["answers"]
    sev = ["cosmetic", "repairable", "major", "write_off"]
    fraud = ["low", "medium", "high"]
    return {
        "peril": {"choice": a["peril"]["choice"], "confidence": a["peril"]["confidence"]},
        "section_covers_peril": {"noul": a["section_covers_peril"]["noul"]},
        "exclusion": {"choice": a["exclusion"]["choice"], "confidence": a["exclusion"]["confidence"]},
        "fault_band": {"level": a["fault_band"]["choice"], "confidence": a["fault_band"]["confidence"]},
        "benefit_courtesy_car": {"noul": a["benefit_courtesy_car"]["noul"]},
        "benefit_legal_expenses": {"noul": a["benefit_legal_expenses"]["noul"]},
        "severity": {"level": sev[min(3, round(a["severity"]["score"]))], "confidence": a["severity"]["confidence"]},
        "evidence_sufficient": {"noul": a["evidence_sufficient"]["noul"]},
        "fraud_risk": {"level": fraud[min(2, round(a["fraud_risk"]["score"]))], "confidence": a["fraud_risk"]["confidence"]},
    }


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- event sink (local file, VastDB when configured)

def record_event(event: dict) -> None:
    event = {"at": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S"), **event}
    with EVENTS.open("a") as f:
        f.write(json.dumps(event) + "\n")
    if env("VASTDB_ENDPOINT"):
        try:
            _vastdb_insert(event)
        except Exception as exc:  # keep the desk working if the store is down

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- footage Q&A (replay)

INTENTS = [
    (r"\b(light|signal|red|green|amber)\b", ("signal",)),
    (r"\b(indicat|blinker|signall)", ("signal",)),
    (r"\b(impact|hit|collid|crash|contact|where)\b", ("impact",)),
    (r"\b(weather|rain|wet|dark|night|light(ing)?|visib)", ("weather", "light", "road")),
    (r"\b(speed|fast|mph|brak|stop(ped)?)\b", ("motion",)),
    (r"\b(give.?way|junction|roundabout|lane|road|marking|sign)\b", ("road",)),
    (r"\b(car|vehicle|van|bus|who|colour|color)\b", ("vehicle",)),
]


def answer(claim: dict, question: str) -> dict:
    q = question.lower()
    findings = claim["findings"]
    hits: list[dict] = []
    for pattern, ks in INTENTS:  # the first intent with matching findings wins
        if re.search(pattern, q):
            hits = [f for f in findings if f["kind"] in ks]
            if hits:
                break
    if re.search(r"\b(speed|mph|fast)\b", q) and not any(f["kind"] == "motion" for f in hits):
        return {"answer": "Not visible. Speed needs GPS, telematics or a second camera; this clip cannot show it.",
                "grounded": False, "citations": []}
    if re.search(r"\bindicat", q):
        ind = [f for f in findings if "indicator" in f["text"].lower()]
        if not ind or ind[0]["conf"] < 0.5:
            return {"answer": "Not visible. Indicators cannot be seen in this footage after the impact.",
                    "grounded": False, "citations": [{"finding": ind[0]["id"]}] if ind else []}
    if not hits:
        return {"answer": "Not visible in this footage. Try asking about the signals, the point of impact, the vehicles or the road.",
                "grounded": False, "citations": []}
    hits.sort(key=lambda f: -f["conf"])
    top = [f for f in hits if f["conf"] >= 0.5][:2] or hits[:1]
    weak = all(f["conf"] < 0.5 for f in top)
    text = " ".join(f["text"] for f in top)
    if weak:
        text = f"Unclear. {text}"
    return {"answer": text, "grounded": not weak, "citations": [{"finding": f["id"]} for f in top]}
    not_covered: list[dict] = []
    branch = ""

    failed = [c for c in checks if not c["pass"]]
    if failed:
        outcome, branch = "reject", "hard_rule_failed"
        for c in failed:
            reasons.append({"text": f"{c['label']}: failed ({c['detail']}).", "cite": c.get("clause")})
        not_covered.append({"name": "Damage to your car", "detail": "Hard-rule check failed, see reasons.", "cite": failed[0].get("clause")})
        covered.append({"name": "Liability to others", "detail": "The third party's claim is still handled under the law.", "cite": "S2"})
    elif evidence_p < 0.5 or fault == "cannot_determine" or jev["fraud_risk"]["level"] == "high" or low:
        outcome, branch = "refer", "uncertain"
        if jev["fraud_risk"]["level"] == "high":
            reasons.append({"text": "Fraud-risk signals are high. A person reviews this; it is not an accusation.", "cite": None})
        if evidence_p < 0.5:
            reasons.append({"text": "Not enough evidence to decide cover yet.", "cite": None})
        if fault == "cannot_determine":
            reasons.append({"text": "Fault cannot be determined from the footage.", "cite": None})
        for k in low:
            reasons.append({"text": f"`{k}` is below the {THRESHOLDS['floor']} confidence floor ({key_conf[k]:.2f}).", "cite": None})
    elif jev["exclusion"]["choice"] != "none" and jev["exclusion"]["confidence"] >= THRESHOLDS["reject"]:
        outcome, branch = "reject", "exclusion"
        clause = jev["exclusion"]["choice"]
        reasons.append({"text": "An exclusion applies.", "cite": clause})
        not_covered.append({"name": "Damage to your car", "detail": "Excluded by the policy wording.", "cite": clause})
    elif covers_p < 0.5 and noul_conf(covers_p) >= THRESHOLDS["reject"]:
        outcome, branch = "reject", "section_not_covered"
        reasons.append({"text": f"{COVER_LABEL[cover]} cover does not include damage to your own car.", "cite": "S1"})
        if fault in ("mostly_at_fault", "fully_at_fault"):
            reasons.append({"text": f"The footage puts the policyholder {FAULT_LABEL[fault].lower()}.", "cite": (claim.get("rules") or [None])[0]})
        not_covered.append({"name": "Damage to your car", "detail": f"Section 1 is not part of {COVER_LABEL[cover].lower()} cover.", "cite": "S1"})
```

```text
### Live cameras

![Live TfL cameras, grouped by the claim they are near](docs/screens/cameras.jpg)

Every claim gets the four Transport for London (TfL) traffic cameras closest to it, with distances. London has about 800 of these cameras, and they post a new picture every 5 to 8 minutes.

![A live camera scanned with YOLO: 1 bus, 10 cars, 2 traffic lights and 1 person, next to an "Attach as evidence" button](docs/screens/live-scan.jpg)

Open a camera and scan its latest picture with YOLO. If it helps, attach it to a claim. The picture gets a fingerprint and goes into the claim's evidence log.

### The incident library
---
| --- | --- | --- |
| London traffic cameras | No key needed (`TFL_APP_KEY` raises TfL's rate limit) | The last saved camera list |
| YOLO scan of a live camera | `YOLO_URL`, or `ultralytics` installed locally | The scan says no detector is connected |
| Boxes on the claim footage | Worked out ahead of time with YOLO11s (`server/tools/detect_stills.py`) | Same |
| Coverage decision | `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` or `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` (Jev) | Recorded Jev answers |
| Questions about the footage | `COSMOS3_REASON_URL` (Cosmos Reason) or `WANDB_API_KEY` (W&B Inference) | Answers built from the findings |
| Incident library | A Jev key | Off |
| Event store | `VASTDB_ENDPOINT`, `VASTDB_ACCESS_KEY` and `VASTDB_SECRET_KEY` | `server/data/events.jsonl` |
---
The scanner is in `server/watch.py`. Here's what it does.

1. About once a minute it asks each camera whether its picture has changed. A picture that hasn't changed costs nothing.
2. A new picture goes to Jev once, with 12 questions in a single request. Is there an incident? What kind? Is a lane blocked? Is the road wet? There are eight more like these, plus a box around the problem.
3. One picture that scores 0.7 or more, with an incident type such as a collision or a breakdown, opens an incident. A second picture confirms it.
4. Two quiet pictures in a row close it. So do 30 minutes with no new picture.

Every judged picture also goes into a daily log. That gives you road conditions and traffic for every camera in London, every few minutes. It all lives in `server/data/library/`, which isn't committed and is served at `/library/`.

| File | What's in it |
| --- | --- |
| `observations-<date>.jsonl` | One line per picture: camera, time, every answer, tokens used |
| `incidents.json` | The incident library (the Export button downloads it) |
| `frames/` and `clips/` | Incident pictures and 10-second clips, each with a SHA-256 hash |

Opened, confirmed, cleared and reviewed incidents also go to `events.jsonl`, and to VastDB once it's set up.

### What it costs

A picture costs about 1,700 Jev tokens, roughly $0.00007. All of London comes to about 7,000 pictures and $0.50 an hour.

### How to control it

---

### Why the threshold is 0.7

In a test, real crash pictures scored between 0.94 and 0.99. The highest normal London picture in the first sweep scored 0.63, and that was a smudged lens. So 0.7 sits in the gap. Some sun glare still gets through, which is why the review buttons are there. The questions and thresholds are all at the top of `server/watch.py`.

## Demo in 90 seconds

1. The inbox has seven claims that need a person. Open PD-0147 (`J`/`K`, then `Enter`).
2. The policyholder's dashcam plays. A blue Vauxhall Mokka pulls out of a give-way junction into her. Click the finding "Blue car broadside across the policyholder's lane" and the clip stops there, with a YOLO box on the car. The two nearest live TfL cameras sit beside it.
3. Ask "Where was the point of impact?" (the answer cites the impact finding). Then ask "How fast was the other car going?" (the answer is "Not visible").
4. The recommendation is accept, partial. The other driver is at fault under Highway Code rule 172, and the courtesy car isn't on her policy. Poodle pays £6,500 now and recovers £6,850 from the other insurer.
5. Open a live camera, scan its latest picture and attach it to the claim. It joins the evidence log with its fingerprint.
6. Press `⌘K` and type "camden". PD-0226 (hit from behind in traffic) can be paid without a handler. PD-0188 (a car cut in from a slip road, then braked hard) has a fraud flag and goes to the special investigations team. In PD-0204 the van driver says he was already on the roundabout, and the rider's helmet camera says he wasn't.
7. Press `G` then `L` for the incident library: the scanner's live feed and the incidents it found today.
8. Open the evidence pack: one printable page with the decision, the findings, the statement check and the file fingerprints.

The amounts in steps 4 and 6 come from the recorded Jev answers. See the next section.

## What doesn't work yet

- Live Jev is stricter than the recorded answers. With a Jev key set, it sends most claims to a person for now.
- The incident scanner has false alarms, mostly sun glare and dirty lenses.
- The Cosmos Reason, W&B Inference and VastDB connections are written but not tested. We didn't have those credentials on the laptop we built this on.

## Where the footage comes from

The claim videos are real UK dashcam and helmet-camera clips sent in to UK Dash Cameras. The originals are in `poodle/media/raw/` (about 90 MB). `server/tools/build_media.py` cuts them into 720p web clips with posters (about 16 MB). The findings, statement checks and Jev answers were written for each clip. The places, dates, people and policies are made up, so the dates burned into the videos don't match the claims.

Live camera pictures come from TfL JamCams. Powered by TfL Open Data.

We also tried generating crash clips. `server/tools/luma_videos.py` makes 5-second CCTV-style clips with Luma Ray2 on Amazon Bedrock, with the camera locked in place. The desk doesn't use them. It plays the real footage. Ray2 only runs in us-west-2, costs $7.50 per clip and needs `aws sso login`.

## Deploying
```

```text
----
def answer(claim: dict, question: str) -> dict:
    q = question.lower()
    findings = claim["findings"]
    hits: list[dict] = []
    for pattern, ks in INTENTS:  # the first intent with matching findings wins
        if re.search(pattern, q):
            hits = [f for f in findings if f["kind"] in ks]
            if hits:
                break
    if re.search(r"\b(speed|mph|fast)\b", q) and not any(f["kind"] == "motion" for f in hits):
        return {"answer": "Not visible. Speed needs GPS, telematics or a second camera; this clip cannot show it.",
                "grounded": False, "citations": []}
    if re.search(r"\bindicat", q):
        ind = [f for f in findings if "indicator" in f["text"].lower()]
        if not ind or ind[0]["conf"] < 0.5:
            return {"answer": "Not visible. Indicators cannot be seen in this footage after the impact.",
                    "grounded": False, "citations": [{"finding": ind[0]["id"]}] if ind else []}
    if not hits:
        return {"answer": "Not visible in this footage. Try asking about the signals, the point of impact, the vehicles or the road.",
                "grounded": False, "citations": []}
    hits.sort(key=lambda f: -f["conf"])
    top = [f for f in hits if f["conf"] >= 0.5][:2] or hits[:1]
    weak = all(f["conf"] < 0.5 for f in top)
    text = " ".join(f["text"] for f in top)
    if weak:
        text = f"Unclear. {text}"
    return {"answer": text, "grounded": not weak, "citations": [{"finding": f["id"]} for f in top]}
```

   "description": "After a crash, a handler watches the dashcam clip, reads the statement and checks the policy by hand. Poodle does that first pass for car insurers. The claim page shows the clip with YOLO11s boxes, timed findings and the driver's statement. Footage answers cite a finding or say \"Not visible\". Every file is SHA-256 hashed; it prints as one evidence pack.\n\nCode runs hard checks on dates, registration, driver and territory, then a decision table pays, refers or rejects. TypeSafe Jev answers nine typed questions per claim (peril, fault, exclusion, fraud), each with a confidence. Under 0.5 on a key answer the claim goes to a person; a Jev-driven reject needs 0.9.\n\nIt also watches about 800 TfL JamCams. Each new still goes to Jev with 12 questions in one call, including a box. Code tracks each camera: a frame at 0.7 opens an incident, a second confirms it, two quiet frames clear it. Stills, 10-second clips, every answer and review verdicts sit in one library. All of London costs about $0.50 an hour.\n\nNVIDIA: Cosmos Reason video Q&A, plus YOLO on the lab endpoint or local YOLO11s. CoreWeave (Weights & Biases): W&B Inference answers from the findings.   ONE SENTENCE (269 chars): Poodle is a claims desk for car insurers that watches the dashcam clip of a crash, sets the driver's statement beside what the camera saw, works out what the policy pays with fixed rules and typed Jev answers, and sends anything it is not sure about to a human handler.
  
  DESCRIPTION (1446 chars):
  Poodle does a claims handler's first pass for car insurers. The claim page shows the dashcam clip with YOLO11s boxes, timed findings and the driver's statement. Answers from the findings cite one or say "Not visible". Every file is SHA-256 hashed and the claim prints as one evidence pack.
  
  Code runs hard checks on dates, registration, driver and territory; a decision table pays, refers or rejects. TypeSafe Jev answers nine typed questions per claim (peril, fault, exclusion, fraud), each with a confidence; without a key the desk replays recorded answers. Under 0.5 on a key answer the claim goes to a person; a Jev-driven reject needs 0.9.
  
  It also watches about 800 TfL JamCams. Each new still gets 12 Jev questions in one call, including a box. A frame at 0.7 opens an incident, a second confirms it, two quiet ones clear it. Stills, 10-second clips, answers and reviews sit in one library. Today's run on all of London cost about $0.70 an hour.
  
  NVIDIA: Cosmos Reason video Q&A and YOLO on the lab endpoint (Ultralytics YOLO11s stands in locally). CoreWeave (Weights & Biases): W&B Inference is wired to answer from the findings. VAST Data: every question, action and incident is wired to VastDB. SpaceXAI (Cursor): Cursor wrote most of the code, Claude Code the idea doc and Jev skill. Lab YOLO, Cosmos, W&B and VastDB switch on from env vars and are untested (no credentials on build day); the desk falls back to replay and a local log.

  ONE SENTENCE (269 chars): Poodle is a claims desk for car insurers that watches the dashcam clip of a crash, sets the driver's statement beside what the camera saw, works out what the policy pays with fixed rules and typed Jev answers, and sends anything it is not sure about to a human handler.
  
  DESCRIPTION (1446 chars):
  Poodle does a claims handler's first pass for car insurers. The claim page shows the dashcam clip with YOLO11s boxes, timed findings and the driver's statement. Answers from the findings cite one or say "Not visible". Every file is SHA-256 hashed and the claim prints as one evidence pack.
  
  Code runs hard checks on dates, registration, driver and territory; a decision table pays, refers or rejects. TypeSafe Jev answers nine typed questions per claim (peril, fault, exclusion, fraud), each with a confidence; without a key the desk replays recorded answers. Under 0.5 on a key answer the claim goes to a person; a Jev-driven reject needs 0.9.
  
  It also watches about 800 TfL JamCams. Each new still gets 12 Jev questions in one call, including a box. A frame at 0.7 opens an incident, a second confirms it, two quiet ones clear it. Stills, 10-second clips, answers and reviews sit in one library. Today's run on all of London cost about $0.70 an hour.
  
  NVIDIA: Cosmos Reason video Q&A and YOLO on the lab endpoint (Ultralytics YOLO11s stands in locally). CoreWeave (Weights & Biases): W&B Inference is wired to answer from the findings. VAST Data: every question, action and incident is wired to VastDB. SpaceXAI (Cursor): Cursor wrote most of the code, Claude Code the idea doc and Jev skill. Lab YOLO, Cosmos, W&B and VastDB switch on from env vars and are untested (no credentials on build day); the desk falls back to replay and a local log.

```text
The amounts in steps 4 and 6 come from the recorded Jev answers. See the next section.

## What doesn't work yet

- Live Jev is stricter than the recorded answers. With a Jev key set, it sends most claims to a person for now.
- The incident scanner has false alarms, mostly sun glare and dirty lenses.
- The Cosmos Reason, W&B Inference and VastDB connections are written but not tested. We didn't have those credentials on the laptop we built this on.

## Where the footage comes from

The claim videos are real UK dashcam and helmet-camera clips sent in to UK Dash Cameras. The originals are in `poodle/media/raw/` (about 90 MB). `server/tools/build_media.py` cuts them into 720p web clips with posters (about 16 MB). The findings, statement checks and Jev answers were written for each clip. The places, dates, people and policies are made up, so the dates burned into the videos don't match the claims.

Live camera pictures come from TfL JamCams. Powered by TfL Open Data.

We also tried generating crash clips. `server/tools/luma_videos.py` makes 5-second CCTV-style clips with Luma Ray2 on Amazon Bedrock, with the camera locked in place. The desk doesn't use them. It plays the real footage. Ray2 only runs in us-west-2, costs $7.50 per clip and needs `aws sso login`.

| `incidents.json` | The incident library (the Export button downloads it) |
| `frames/` and `clips/` | Incident pictures and 10-second clips, each with a SHA-256 hash |

Opened, confirmed, cleared and reviewed incidents also go to `events.jsonl`, and to VastDB once it's set up.

### What it costs

A picture costs about 1,700 Jev tokens, roughly $0.00007. All of London comes to about 7,000 pictures and $0.50 an hour.
```

```text
"""Background incident scanner: every live TfL JamCam, judged by Jev, kept as a library.

The app starts it when a Jev key is set (POODLE_WATCH=off turns it off):

- poll each camera's still with a conditional GET; S3 answers 304 until TfL publishes
  a new frame, which happens every 5 to 8 minutes per camera;
- send each new frame to Jev once, with every question below batched in one request;
- code turns the typed answers into incidents: opened by one flagged frame, confirmed
  by a second, cleared after two quiet frames or 30 minutes without a frame.

Runtime data lives in data/library/ (gitignored) and is served at /library/:
  observations-<date>.jsonl  one row per judged frame: the data mine
  incidents.json             the incident library
  frames/, clips/            incident stills and the camera's 10 s clips, with SHA-256
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import base64
import hashlib
import json
import random
import time
import uuid
from collections import Counter, OrderedDict, deque
from datetime import date, datetime
from email.utils import parsedate_to_datetime
from pathlib import Path

import httpx

from . import services, tfl

LIBRARY = Path(services.env("POODLE_LIBRARY_DIR") or Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "data" / "library")
USD_PER_TOKEN = 0.042 / 1_000_000

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- questions and thresholds
# One reviewable place for what Jev is asked about each frame and how code acts on it.
# Thresholds are starting points from a probe on crash stills and live frames; calibrate
# them on the review labels the desk collects.

QUESTIONS = {
    "usable": {
        "type": "noul", "instructions": "Can the road and the vehicles on it be seen in `frame`?",
        "criteria": {"true": "the carriageway is visible clearly enough to judge what is happening on it",
                     "false": "the frame is blank, grey, a 'camera unavailable' card, pointing at a wall or the sky, "
                              "too dark to see the road, or the lens is covered by rain, glare or dirt"}},
    "incident": {
        "type": "noul", "instructions": "Does `frame` show a road incident happening now?",
        "criteria": {"true": "a collision, a damaged, overturned or burning vehicle, a vehicle stopped across a live lane "
                             "or at an odd angle, emergency services working on the road, debris or a fallen object on "
                             "the carriageway, flooding, or a person lying in the road",
                     "false": "ordinary traffic, including queues, parked cars, buses at stops, vehicles waiting at lights, "
                              "roadworks behind barriers, and vehicles stopped at the kerb"}},
    "kind": {
        "type": "choice", "instructions": "What is the main thing happening on the road in `frame`?",
        "criteria": {
            "collision": "a crash: vehicles in contact, a damaged or overturned vehicle, or wreckage",
            "breakdown": "one vehicle stopped in a live lane with hazard lights, a raised bonnet or a tow truck",
            "emergency_response": "police, ambulance or fire vehicles stopped on the road at a scene",
            "obstruction": "debris, a fallen tree, a spilled load or another object blocking the carriageway",
            "flooding": "standing water covering part of the carriageway",
            "fire_or_smoke": "flames or smoke from a vehicle or the roadside",
            "person_in_road": "a person lying, standing or walking in a live traffic lane away from a crossing",
            "roadworks": "planned works: cones, barriers, works vehicles or a lane closed for maintenance",
            "congestion": "slow or stationary queues with no visible cause",
            "normal": "traffic moving normally, or an empty road",
            "unclear": "the frame is too dark, blurred, obstructed or blank to tell",
            "other": "something else unusual on the road"}},
    "severity": {
        "type": "score", "instructions": "How urgently should a traffic control room operator look at `frame`?",
        "criteria": ["nothing to act on: normal traffic",
                     "worth noting: a stopped vehicle, a queue or works that is not blocking traffic",
                     "act now: a lane is blocked by a collision, breakdown, obstruction or emergency scene",
                     "major: a serious crash, a fire, an overturned vehicle, people hurt, or the road is closed"]},
    "emergency_vehicle": {"type": "noul", "instructions": "Is a police car, ambulance or fire engine visible in `frame`?"},
    "damaged_vehicle": {
        "type": "noul",
        "instructions": "Is a vehicle in `frame` visibly damaged, overturned, on fire, or facing against the flow of traffic?"},
    "lane_blocked": {
        "type": "noul",
        "instructions": "Is a traffic lane in `frame` blocked by a stopped vehicle, debris, people or emergency services, "
                        "so that traffic has to go around it?",
        "criteria": {"true": "a lane is obstructed by something that is not part of normal traffic",
                     "false": "vehicles waiting at lights or in a queue, parked in bays, or at a bus stop; or no lane is blocked"}},
    "people_in_road": {
        "type": "noul", "instructions": "Are people standing or walking in a traffic lane in `frame`, away from a pedestrian crossing?"},
    "traffic": {
        "type": "score", "instructions": "How much traffic is on the road in `frame`?",
        "criteria": ["empty road", "light traffic with large gaps", "busy, vehicles close together",
                     "nose-to-tail queue filling the lanes"]},
    "surface": {
        "type": "choice", "instructions": "What is the condition of the road surface in `frame`?",
        "criteria": {"dry": "dry road", "wet": "wet road, puddles or reflections on the surface",
                     "snow_or_ice": "snow or ice on the road", "unclear": "cannot see the surface"}},
    "light": {
        "type": "choice", "instructions": "What is the lighting in `frame`?",
        "criteria": {"daylight": "daylight", "dusk": "dusk or dawn", "night_lit": "night with street lights",
                     "dark": "night without useful light"}},
    "where": {"type": "box",
              "instructions": "the collision, damaged vehicle, stopped vehicle, obstruction or emergency scene in `frame`"},
}

THRESHOLDS = {
    "usable": 0.5,  # below: the view cannot be judged, so the frame neither extends nor clears an incident
    "open": 0.7,    # `incident` needed to open an incident, or to count towards confirming one
    "keep": 0.5,    # `incident` that keeps an open incident alive
    "box": 0.3,     # weakest box confidence worth drawing
}
INCIDENT_KINDS = {"collision", "breakdown", "emergency_response", "obstruction", "flooding", "fire_or_smoke",
                  "person_in_road", "other"}
CONFIRM_FRAMES = 2       # flagged frames that confirm an incident
CLEAR_FRAMES = 2         # quiet frames in a row that clear it
STALE_SECONDS = 30 * 60  # an open incident with no frame for this long is cleared
MAX_FRAMES = 12          # stills kept per incident
MAX_CLIPS = 3            # 10 s clips kept per incident
POLL_IDLE = 60           # seconds between checks while a camera's still is unchanged
POLL_AFTER_NEW = 210     # TfL refreshes each camera every 5 to 8 minutes
FETCH_CONCURRENCY = 12
CENTRE = (51.5073, -0.1276)  # Charing Cross: POODLE_WATCH_LIMIT keeps the cameras nearest to it


def flagged(o: dict) -> bool:
    return o["usable"] >= THRESHOLDS["usable"] and o["incident"] >= THRESHOLDS["open"] and o["kind"] in INCIDENT_KINDS


def compact(a: dict) -> dict:
    """The typed answers for one frame, flattened into an observation row."""
    r = lambda x: round(float(x), 3)  # noqa: E731
    return {
        "usable": r(a["usable"]["noul"]), "incident": r(a["incident"]["noul"]),
        "kind": a["kind"]["choice"], "kindConf": r(a["kind"]["confidence"]),
        "severity": r(a["severity"]["score"]),
        "emergency": r(a["emergency_vehicle"]["noul"]), "damaged": r(a["damaged_vehicle"]["noul"]),
        "blocked": r(a["lane_blocked"]["noul"]), "people": r(a["people_in_road"]["noul"]),
        "traffic": r(a["traffic"]["score"]), "surface": a["surface"]["choice"], "light": a["light"]["choice"],
    }
```

```text
"""Sponsor-stack adapters. Each switches on from env vars; without them Poodle runs
in replay mode and reports that in /api/health.

Unverified against the event stack (no credentials on the build laptop): the YOLO,
Cosmos, W&B Inference, Jev and VastDB request shapes follow docs/hack-plan.md and the
jev-decisions skill. Check them on the team VM before the demo.

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import base64
import json
import os
import time
from pathlib import Path

import httpx

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
EVENTS = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "data" / "events.jsonl"


def load_dotenv(path: Path) -> None:
    """Read KEY=VALUE lines into the environment. Variables already set win, blank values are skipped."""
    if not path.exists():
        return
    for line in path.read_text().splitlines():
        line = line.strip()
        if not line or line.startswith("#") or "=" not in line:
            continue
        key, _, value = line.partition("=")
        key = key.removeprefix("export ").strip()
        value = value.strip().strip("\"'")
        if key and value and key not in os.environ:
            os.environ[key] = value


load_dotenv(ROOT / ".env")


def env(name: str) -> str | None:
    value = os.environ.get(name)
    return value.strip() if value and value.strip() else None


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- detector

_local_model = None


def _local_yolo_available() -> bool:
    try:
        import ultralytics  # noqa: F401
        return True
    except Exception:
        return False


LOCAL_YOLO = _local_yolo_available()
----


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- Jev (typed coverage answers)

FAULT_OPTIONS = {
    "not_at_fault": "the policyholder did nothing to cause the collision",
    "shared_fault": "both drivers contributed",
    "mostly_at_fault": "the policyholder caused most of it",
    "fully_at_fault": "the policyholder caused it",
    "cannot_determine": "the facts do not show who caused it",
}


def jev_questions(policy: dict, wording: dict) -> dict:
    exclusions = {k: v["text"] for k, v in wording.items() if k.startswith("E")}
    exclusions["none"] = "no exclusion applies"
    return {
        "peril": {"type": "choice", "instructions": "What happened in `facts`?", "criteria": {
            "collision_with_vehicle": "a collision with another vehicle", "collision_with_object": "hit an object",
            "collision_with_pedestrian_or_cyclist": "hit a person on foot or a cyclist", "theft": "theft",
            "vandalism": "vandalism", "fire": "fire", "weather": "weather damage", "glass_only": "glass only", "other": "something else"}},
        "section_covers_peril": {"type": "noul", "instructions": "Does Section 1 in `policy` cover damage to the policyholder's own car for this incident under `policy.cover`?"},
        "exclusion": {"type": "choice", "instructions": "Which exclusion in `policy` do `facts` trigger?", "criteria": exclusions},
        "fault_band": {"type": "choice", "instructions": "How much did the policyholder contribute to the collision in `facts`?", "criteria": FAULT_OPTIONS},
        "benefit_courtesy_car": {"type": "noul", "instructions": "Would the policyholder need a courtesy car while their car is repaired, given `facts`?"},
        "benefit_legal_expenses": {"type": "noul", "instructions": "Do `facts` give the policyholder uninsured losses to recover from another driver?"},
        "severity": {"type": "score", "instructions": "How badly damaged is the policyholder's car in `facts`?",
                     "criteria": ["cosmetic scuffs", "repairable damage", "major structural damage", "likely write-off"]},
        "evidence_sufficient": {"type": "noul", "instructions": "Do `facts` contain enough evidence to decide cover without asking for more?"},
        "fraud_risk": {"type": "score", "instructions": "How strongly do `facts` match staged-collision patterns?",
                       "criteria": ["no staged-collision signs", "some signs worth a look", "strong staged-collision signs"]},
    }


def jev_target() -> tuple[str, str, str] | None:
    """(base URL, key, model) for Jev, or None when no key is set."""
    key = env("TYPESAFE_API_KEY") or env("OPENROUTER_API_KEY")
    if not key:
        return None
    direct = bool(env("TYPESAFE_API_KEY"))
    base = env("JEV_BASE_URL") or ("https://api.typesafe.ai" if direct else "https://openrouter.ai/api")
    model = env("JEV_MODEL") or ("jev-1.14.0" if direct else "typesafe/jev-1.14")
    return base, key, model


async def jev_decide(client: httpx.AsyncClient, claim: dict, policy: dict, wording: dict) -> dict | None:
    target = jev_target()
    if not target:
        return None
    base, key, model = target
    state = {
        "facts": {"findings": [f["text"] for f in claim["findings"]], "statement": claim["statement"]["text"],
                  "driver": claim["driver"], "estimate": claim.get("estimate")},
        "policy": {"cover": policy["cover"], "addOns": policy["addOns"],
                   "wording": {k: v["text"] for k, v in wording.items()}},
    }
    r = await client.post(f"{base}/v1/systemone", headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {key}"}, timeout=15,
                          json={"model": model, "state": state, "questions": jev_questions(policy, wording)})
    r.raise_for_status()
    a = r.json()["answers"]
    sev = ["cosmetic", "repairable", "major", "write_off"]
    fraud = ["low", "medium", "high"]
    return {
        "peril": {"choice": a["peril"]["choice"], "confidence": a["peril"]["confidence"]},
        "section_covers_peril": {"noul": a["section_covers_peril"]["noul"]},
        "exclusion": {"choice": a["exclusion"]["choice"], "confidence": a["exclusion"]["confidence"]},
        "fault_band": {"level": a["fault_band"]["choice"], "confidence": a["fault_band"]["confidence"]},
        "benefit_courtesy_car": {"noul": a["benefit_courtesy_car"]["noul"]},
        "benefit_legal_expenses": {"noul": a["benefit_legal_expenses"]["noul"]},
        "severity": {"level": sev[min(3, round(a["severity"]["score"]))], "confidence": a["severity"]["confidence"]},
        "evidence_sufficient": {"noul": a["evidence_sufficient"]["noul"]},
        "fraud_risk": {"level": fraud[min(2, round(a["fraud_risk"]["score"]))], "confidence": a["fraud_risk"]["confidence"]},
    }


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- event sink (local file, VastDB when configured)

def record_event(event: dict) -> None:
    event = {"at": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S"), **event}
    with EVENTS.open("a") as f:
        f.write(json.dumps(event) + "\n")
    if env("VASTDB_ENDPOINT"):
        try:
            _vastdb_insert(event)
        except Exception as exc:  # keep the desk working if the store is down
            print("vastdb insert failed:", exc)


def _vastdb_insert(event: dict) -> None:
    import pyarrow as pa
    import vastdb

    session = vastdb.connect(endpoint=env("VASTDB_ENDPOINT"), access=env("VASTDB_ACCESS_KEY"), secret=env("VASTDB_SECRET_KEY"))
    columns = pa.schema([("at", pa.string()), ("claim", pa.string()), ("kind", pa.string()), ("payload", pa.string())])
    with session.transaction() as tx:
        bucket = tx.bucket(env("VASTDB_BUCKET") or "poodle")
        schema = bucket.schema("poodle", fail_if_missing=False) or bucket.create_schema("poodle")
        table = schema.table("events", fail_if_missing=False) or schema.create_table("events", columns)
        table.insert(pa.table({"at": [event["at"]], "claim": [event.get("claim", "")], "kind": [event.get("kind", "")],
                               "payload": [json.dumps(event)]}))


def services_status(tfl_status: dict) -> list[dict]:
    def s(id_, name, role, live, live_text, fallback):
        return {"id": id_, "name": name, "role": role, "status": "live" if live else "replay", "detail": live_text if live else fallback}

    yolo_live = bool(env("YOLO_URL")) or LOCAL_YOLO
    try:
        import vastdb  # noqa: F401
        vastdb_sdk = True
    except Exception:
        vastdb_sdk = False
    vastdb_fallback = "SDK not installed (pip install vastdb pyarrow)" if env("VASTDB_ENDPOINT") else "Local event log"
    return [
        s("tfl", "TfL JamCams", "Live London cameras", tfl_status["ok"], f"{tfl_status['count']} live", "Snapshot (feed unreachable)"),
        s("yolo", "YOLO11", "Detection on frames", yolo_live, "Event stack" if env("YOLO_URL") else "Local yolo11s", "Precomputed boxes"),
        s("cosmos", "Cosmos Reason", "Video reasoning", bool(env("COSMOS3_REASON_URL")), "Event stack", "Recorded findings"),
        s("jev", "TypeSafe Jev", "Typed coverage answers", bool(env("TYPESAFE_API_KEY") or env("OPENROUTER_API_KEY")), "jev-1.14.0", "Seeded answers"),
        s("llm", "W&B Inference", "Answers in plain English", bool(env("WANDB_API_KEY")), env("POODLE_LLM_MODEL") or "Llama 3.3 70B", "Rule-based answers"),
        s("vastdb", "VastDB", "Evidence and events store", bool(env("VASTDB_ENDPOINT")) and vastdb_sdk, "Writing events", vastdb_fallback),
    ]
```

```text
"""Coverage decision and footage Q&A for Poodle.

Three layers, as in docs/IDEA.md:
- code owns hard rules, dates, arithmetic and the decision table (this file);
- Jev supplies typed judgments (peril, exclusion, fault band, ...). Without a key the
  seeded answers in data/claims.json stand in and the record says so;
- an LLM only writes prose (Q&A answers when W&B Inference is configured).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import re
from datetime import date, datetime
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
DATA = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "data"
WEB = ROOT / "poodle"

THRESHOLDS = {"floor": 0.5, "reject": 0.9}
UK_BOX = (49.8, 60.9, -8.7, 1.8)  # lat min, lat max, lon min, lon max

COVER_LABEL = {
    "comprehensive": "Comprehensive",
    "third_party_fire_theft": "Third party, fire and theft",
    "third_party_only": "Third party only",
}
FAULT_LABEL = {
    "not_at_fault": "Not at fault",
    "shared_fault": "Shared fault",
    "mostly_at_fault": "Mostly at fault",
    "fully_at_fault": "Fully at fault",
    "cannot_determine": "Cannot determine",
}
OUTCOME_LABEL = {"accept": "Accept", "partial": "Accept, partial", "reject": "Reject", "refer": "Refer to handler"}


def load_json(name: str):
    return json.loads((DATA / name).read_text())


def noul_conf(p: float) -> float:
    return round(abs(2 * p - 1), 2)


def sha256(path: Path) -> str:
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    with path.open("rb") as f:
        for chunk in iter(lambda: f.read(1 << 16), b""):
            h.update(chunk)
    return h.hexdigest()


def money(v: float | int | None) -> str:
    return "—" if v is None else f"£{v:,.0f}"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- hard rules (code)
----

    branch = ""

    failed = [c for c in checks if not c["pass"]]
    if failed:
        outcome, branch = "reject", "hard_rule_failed"
        for c in failed:
            reasons.append({"text": f"{c['label']}: failed ({c['detail']}).", "cite": c.get("clause")})
        not_covered.append({"name": "Damage to your car", "detail": "Hard-rule check failed, see reasons.", "cite": failed[0].get("clause")})
        covered.append({"name": "Liability to others", "detail": "The third party's claim is still handled under the law.", "cite": "S2"})
    elif evidence_p < 0.5 or fault == "cannot_determine" or jev["fraud_risk"]["level"] == "high" or low:
        outcome, branch = "refer", "uncertain"
        if jev["fraud_risk"]["level"] == "high":
            reasons.append({"text": "Fraud-risk signals are high. A person reviews this; it is not an accusation.", "cite": None})
        if evidence_p < 0.5:
            reasons.append({"text": "Not enough evidence to decide cover yet.", "cite": None})
        if fault == "cannot_determine":
            reasons.append({"text": "Fault cannot be determined from the footage.", "cite": None})
        for k in low:
            reasons.append({"text": f"`{k}` is below the {THRESHOLDS['floor']} confidence floor ({key_conf[k]:.2f}).", "cite": None})
    elif jev["exclusion"]["choice"] != "none" and jev["exclusion"]["confidence"] >= THRESHOLDS["reject"]:
        outcome, branch = "reject", "exclusion"
        clause = jev["exclusion"]["choice"]
        reasons.append({"text": "An exclusion applies.", "cite": clause})
        not_covered.append({"name": "Damage to your car", "detail": "Excluded by the policy wording.", "cite": clause})
    elif covers_p < 0.5 and noul_conf(covers_p) >= THRESHOLDS["reject"]:
        outcome, branch = "reject", "section_not_covered"

        if fault in ("mostly_at_fault", "fully_at_fault"):
```
